prompt:
An original, severely abstract dark cubist mural in compressed shallow space, painted as one rough surface using only charcoal-black, white, chalk and ash-gray. Strictly monochrome: no red, blue, yellow, ochre, brown, beige, sepia or any other color. Build the image from several large, rounded, swelling and crescent-shaped masses that overlap and interlock across foreground, middle ground and background; let broad curved contours and irregular organic silhouettes dominate. Use bent arcs and sweeping bands alongside sharp breaks. Show three connected actions in the same instant: the fictional protagonist Márton Kádár in a contemplative pose, a secondary figure of an abstract network symbol reacting as light or observation, and the setting showing compressed interlocking shapes symbolizing the European Union member states as a network symbolizing political union and regulation. Make the forms collide, lean, press, pull or flow into one another so the whole canvas carries the event. Fracture faces into displaced masks and mismatched features; distort bodies into broad overlapping forms. Keep Márton Kádár and main action large and unmistakable, with supporting action legible but secondary. Use raw charcoal, broken brush marks, scraped pigment, worn plaster and layered tonal transitions across black, white and gray. The article-photo reference supplies subject matter only: discard its color, realism, lighting, exact framing, poses and real faces; redraw the underlying event as an invented mural. No flags, maps, emblems or readable text. The image API receives only reference image 1: the selected masked character crop, used only for Márton Kádár’s abstract appearance and gesture. No complete painting reference is supplied. Keep figures and setting fused into one unstable painted surface. Absolutely no photorealism, lifelike skin, naturalistic anatomy, camera effects, glossy finish, copied symbols or copied layout.

Scene-specific staging: Look down from above. Show the protagonist seated or crouched and arranged diagonally across the ground plane, with hands close to the body and large curved masses around them. The protagonist reference supplies identity only: ignore its exact pose, raised arms, body silhouette, scale and placement. Make this pose and camera view clearly different from every other scene in this sequence. Reference image 1 is the selected masked figure; redraw its abstract protagonist identity, never paste it. Reference image 2 is the article photograph for subject matter only; ignore its colors, realism, lighting, photographic texture, framing, poses and identifiable faces. Redraw the underlying event as fictional cubist forms using only black, white and gray; never reproduce a real person, photo composition, logos or text.
